criteria.adapter_held_service: The late:: operations execute against a LateOccurrenceService instance the i03 adapter constructs and owns: late.ts is duplicated into runtime/test-support/slices/i03/ without behavioral change (direct import is prohibited by the ship boundary), and each owner-first catalogue call under a new NT-I03 admission tag runs the corresponding method synchronously in-process. Rejection vocabulary maps onto failures: swap/lookup problems (wrong-owner, stale-handle, not-found) surface test::stale_handle, while malformed input, capability, ordering, and bound violations surface late::late_fault with verbatim kind and message. Ordinary Can gains the five closed word sets, thin wrappers, and a worked select/enroll/gate/emit/terminal/observe/lease/outcome roundtrip. This treats K06 as what its header claims: inert local mechanics in the I04 doubles tradition, with genuine P09/P11 authority arriving under separate namespaces later.
criteria.defer_mechanics_inert_facts: No executable late behavior merges now. The catalogue gains late:: record shapes for every fact family plus word-set predicates, and the Can surface validates documents without running them. The twelve-method service remains a host-side tool exactly as K06 shipped it, mirroring how I02 left the K05 witness out of the catalogue. Executable lease and gate semantics then arrive only with their true owners (P09 for workspace leases, P11 for recovery gating), eliminating any chance that local doubles are mistaken for production authority. The I03 card is satisfied in its static half (catalogue delta, helpers, example); the dynamic half is an explicit later merge.
criteria.external_n_dispatch: Candidate calls to late:: operations become JSON envelopes delivered to the external N owner through injected dispatch whose default rejects, exactly as I01 and I11 adapters do. The N side owns all participant, gate, event, lease, and outcome state once P14 qualifies it; before that every late call fails with an unbound-transport error rather than computing anything. Can helpers and the example follow the I01 layout (vocabulary, wrappers, roundtrip), but no assertions can execute until the owner exists. This removes the double-versus-authority dilemma by refusing to compute locally at all.

i03_late_honesty_shape.instructions: K06 shipped an in-memory late-occurrence engine whose facts mirror the future P09/P11 owners without being them. For the I03 merge, should the candidate execute that engine locally in the adapter, address it as a future N-owner service through throwing-by-default dispatch, or merge only its inert fact shapes and word sets while leaving execution to the true owners? Consider: the engine is deterministic local mechanics with 30 passing checks and no external dependencies; its lease/gate vocabulary intentionally echoes P09/P11, creating a possible confusion between the double and the authority; I04 set the adapter-held precedent for doubles while I01/I11 set the external-dispatch precedent for N-resident state; the I03 card demands catalogue growth plus Can helpers and an example; P14 is blocked so nothing merged can earn execution credit yet; all three stagings stay provisional.
